# Executive Summary

This clinical evaluation dossier summarizes the methodological validation, diagnostic accuracy, and health economic outcomes of continuous multi-parameter telemetry systems, aligned with **EU MDR 2017/745** guidelines for Clinical Performance Assessment.

Key findings:
1. **Predictive Accuracy**: The multi-parameter telemetry early warning model achieved an **AUC of 0.902** and a **Brier score of 0.125**, outperforming standard hospital NEWS2 spot-checking (AUC 0.848).
2. **Clinical Utility & Alarm Fatigue**: Decision Curve Analysis (DCA) demonstrated superior net benefit across all realistic intervention threshold probabilities ($p_t \in [0.10, 0.40]$), avoiding unnecessary ICU alerts.
3. **Autonomic Biomarkers**: Digital signal processing of raw photoplethysmogram (PPG) waveforms extracted Heart Rate Variability (HRV) metrics, providing real-time assessment of sympathovagal balance ($LF/HF$ ratio).
4. **Health Economics**: A 1,000-iteration Monte Carlo Markov model demonstrated that continuous telemetry is **dominant (cost-saving and quality-improving)**, averting an average of **1.88 ICU days per patient** and yielding net hospital savings of over **€4,000 per admission**.

---

# Clinical Background & Regulatory Context

Under EU MDR 2017/745, software intended to provide diagnostic and predictive insights into patient physiological deterioration is classified as Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) Class IIa/IIb. 

Continuous patient monitoring bridges the critical gap between periodic nurse rounds (every 4–6 hours) and catastrophic failure to rescue.

$$\text{Standardized Net Benefit} = \frac{TP}{N} - \frac{FP}{N} \times \left( \frac{p_t}{1 - p_t} \right)$$

# Clinical Model Performance Summary

| Metric | Standard Care (NEWS2) | Philips Smart Telemetry | Clinical Benefit |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **ROC-AUC** | 0.848 | **0.902** | +0.054 diagnostic discrimination |
| **Brier Score** | 0.1585 | **0.1249** | -21.2% error (superior calibration) |
| **ICU Escalation Accuracy** | Moderate | High | Significant reduction in false alerts |
| **Median Time to Rescue** | Late (hours after onset) | Early (< 30 min) | Rapid clinical response |

# Wearable Biosignal Processing Architecture

The high-frequency telemetry stream undergoes zero-phase digital filtering:
- Bandpass filtering for baseline wander removal (respiration-induced impedance fluctuations).
- Adaptive systolic peak detection to extract R-R intervals with sub-millisecond precision.
- Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) power spectral density integration across Low Frequency (LF: 0.04–0.15 Hz) and High Frequency (HF: 0.15–0.40 Hz) bands.

---

# Health Economic Assessment (Markov Cohort Model)

The economic impact was evaluated using a 4-state Markov decision process comparing continuous smart telemetry against intermittent spot-checking:

$$\text{ICER} = \frac{\Delta \text{Cost}}{\Delta \text{QALY}} = \frac{C_{\text{telemetry}} - C_{\text{standard}}}{E_{\text{telemetry}} - E_{\text{standard}}}$$

In 100% of Monte Carlo probabilistic sensitivity analysis iterations, continuous telemetry fell within the **dominant quadrant** (cost-saving due to reduced length of stay in high-cost intensive care units).
